question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹319.60. Approximately, at what price should he sell the article to make a 25% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Round off the **Cost Price** ₹319.60 to the nearest simple value, which is ₹320.

**Profit percentage** = 25% = 1/4 of the Cost Price.

Profit = 320 ÷ 4 = ₹80.

**Selling Price** = Cost Price + Profit = 320 + 80 = ₹400.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** = ₹319.60

**Profit Percentage** = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit %)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b4ce05b50a9517ef07cb5ab356c02f9e0936f01d66a9b3413549cdc4f5a5e15.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 319.60 × (100 + 25)/100

⇒ SP = 319.60 × 125/100

⇒ SP = 319.60 × 5/4

⇒ SP = 79.90 × 5

⇒ SP = ₹399.50

⇒ Since the question asks for the approximate price, SP ≈ ₹400.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP)

The price at which an article is purchased. Profit or loss is always calculated on this base value unless stated otherwise.

Selling Price (SP)

The price at which an article is sold. It is calculated as SP = CP + Profit or SP = CP − Loss.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. These percentages represent the gain or loss relative to the initial investment.
